title: Anti-Bullying & Cyber Safety
description: Learn how to stand up against bullies, both in the schoolyard and online, and protect your mental health.

scenes.text: You see a group of students laughing at a younger student in the hallway. They are knocking his books out of his hands. You are watching from a distance.
What is the role of a 'Bystander'?

choices.text: Someone who watches the bullying happen but does nothing.
choices.feedbackText: Correct. But we want you to be an 'Upstander'—someone who safely intervenes or gets help!

choices.text: Someone who joins in and helps the bullies.
choices.feedbackText: That would make them a bully too! A bystander is someone who just watches without acting.

scenes.text: You want to be an Upstander. The bullies are much older than you. What is the SAFEST way to help within 15 seconds?

choices.text: Run up and start fighting the older students.
choices.feedbackText: Never put yourself in physical danger! That will just make things worse.

choices.text: Quietly record a video on your phone.
choices.feedbackText: Recording videos can sometimes violate privacy or get you in trouble. It's better to act directly by getting help.

choices.text: Run to the nearest teacher's lounge and get an adult.
choices.feedbackText: Exactly! Getting a trusted adult is the most effective and safest way to stop physical bullying.

scenes.text: You get a teacher who immediately stops the bullies. The younger student thanks you later. You learn that speaking up is the strongest shield against bullying.
